Balanced training/validation/testing split

Source: R/balanced_initial_validation_split.R
balanced_initial_validation_split.Rd

balanced_initial_validation_split() makes one three-way split in which the training, validation, and testing sets are similar on several variables at once. Use rsample::training(), rsample::validation(), and rsample::testing() to get the three data sets, and rsample::validation_set() to tune on the validation set.

Usage

balanced_initial_validation_split(
  data,
  prop = c(0.6, 0.2),
  balance = NULL,
  exact = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  method = "anticlust",
  options = list(),
  na = "error",
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

prop

A vector of two proportions: the first for the training set and the second for the validation set. The rest of the data goes to the testing set. With group, these are proportions of groups. With method = "twinning", each of the three proportions must be a multiple of 1/m for one whole number m up to 20, for example c(0.6, 0.2) (m = 5) or c(0.5, 0.25) (m = 4).

balance

<tidy-select> Columns to balance across the sets. Numeric columns are standardized. So are Date, POSIXct, and difftime columns, as numbers of days or seconds. Factor, character, and logical columns become one indicator column per level.

exact

<tidy-select> Categorical columns to stratify exactly. Each combination of levels is one stratum. In each stratum, the count in every set is the floor or the ceiling of its proportional share, based on the actual size of that set. For folds, the counts of a stratum also differ by at most one over the folds whenever both rules can hold at once. With group, these counts are numbers of groups, not rows. exact does the job of strata in rsample, but it takes several columns and its counts are exact. Numeric columns with whole-number values are treated as categories. Put continuous columns in balance, or use cut() to make a factor if you need exact counts within ranges. A stratum whose share of the smallest set is under one row (or group) can be missing from some sets. If more than half of the strata are missing from at least one set, you get a warning.

group

<tidy-select> One column with group IDs. All rows of a group go to the same set. See Details.

method

The balancing method: "anticlust", "twinning", "rerandomize", or "interaction". See Details.

options

A named list of options for the method. See Details.

na

What to do with missing values in the balance and exact columns. "error" (the default) stops with an error. "include" balances on which values are missing; see Missing values. The group column must not have missing values either way.

...

Not used. Must be empty.

Value

A three_way_split object with class balanced_initial_validation_split and initial_validation_split.

Details

The three sets are made in one pass, so each one is balanced against the other two. rsample's rsample::initial_validation_split() instead splits off the training set first and then splits the rest.

The methods, options, and group handling are the same as for balanced_vfold_cv(). With method = "twinning", the data are split into m similar parts with twinning::multiplet(), and each set gets a whole number of parts. strategy 2 needs m to be a power of 2. Strata with fewer than 2 * m rows (or groups) are split at random.

Use with tune

rsample::validation_set() turns the split into an rset for tune::tune_grid() and tune::fit_resamples(). tune::last_fit() (tune 1.1.2 or later) takes the split itself and fits on the training set, or on the training and validation sets with add_validation_set = TRUE.

If a workflow has a postprocessor that must be trained, tune splits the training set again. Through rsample::validation_set(), rsample makes that inner split at random, without balancing. tune::last_fit() can't train such a postprocessor on any three-way split, including those from rsample::initial_validation_split() (as of tune 2.1.0).

Calling rsample::internal_calibration_split() on this split yourself gives a balanced split of the training set. As in rsample, prop[1] / sum(prop) of the training set goes to the first part and the rest to the calibration set. With method = "twinning", this share is rounded to the nearest 1 - 1/r (or 1/r, below 1/2) for a whole number r, for example 14/17 to 5/6. As in rsample, if the training set can't be split, you get a warning and an empty calibration set.

See also

balanced_initial_split(), balance_check()

Examples

set.seed(1)
split <- balanced_initial_validation_split(
  mtcars,
  prop = c(0.6, 0.2),
  balance = c(mpg, hp, wt),
  exact = am
)
split
#> # Balanced training/validation/testing split (anticlust), balancing mpg, hp, wt,
#> # stratified by am
#> <Training/Validation/Testing/Total>
#> <19/7/6/32>
balance_check(split)
#> # Balance check: 2 splits, 4 variables
#> # 2 of 2 splits have a variable with |SMD| > 0.1, mean energy distance 0.32
#> 
#> id          max |SMD|  variable  mean |SMD|  over 0.1  energy
#> Validation      0.286  am: 0         0.104        2/4   0.408
#> Testing         0.159  am: 0         0.0839       2/4   0.232
#> 
#> # summary() gives this table as a tibble, and tibble::as_tibble() gives all
#> # 12 rows.
rsample::validation_set(split)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   splits         id        
#>   <list>         <chr>     
#> 1 <split [19/7]> validation
